harbor_p03_001.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_001.text: The controlled inventory began near the end of the third week, after the carpenter approved the replacement access walkway. Rain had stopped, leaving every warehouse roof the color of old pewter. Yan Su walked the ordinary crew through their handling positions before the commercial clerk opened the numbered forms. Sui Yan checked protective clothing and the marked sample locations. Yue stood at the dry table assigned to worker-property references. She could smell brine from the hold, but the air carried none of the drama rumor had promised.

harbor_p03_002.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_002.text: The first items brought into the sorting shed were damaged sacks, lifted by the repaired shore tackle within its rating. The crew placed them on shallow trays rather than onto clean cargo. A licensed handler sampled residue where required. Miao watched every movement and objected when a sack bearing his merchant's mark entered the uncertain group. The clerk explained that the mark identified a claim, while the handling condition determined its present location. Miao could dispute ownership without directing a worker to put an unsafe sack elsewhere.

harbor_p03_003.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_003.text: Yue's first property entry was a blue coat wrapped inside a grain sack. He Jun had described the coat's patched left pocket and a repaired toggle before seeing it. The commercial clerk compared the description with the inventory and recorded the match. It remained a provisional identification until the competing cargo claim, if any, could be addressed. Nobody had claimed the coat yet. He Jun stood outside the working lane with his sister and looked cold enough to make every additional minute seem personally unreasonable.

harbor_p03_004.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_004.text: A carved wooden spoon lay with the coat. He Jun had not listed it, though He Ming recognized their mother's work. The clerk asked him whether it was his. He said his mother had sent it without telling him. He Ming laughed, then began to cry. She explained that their mother believed food tasted strange from purchased spoons. The clerk allowed them a moment before returning to the entry. An overlooked spoon could explain a bundle's contents. It could also remind two quarrelling people that somebody had packed for both of them.

harbor_p03_005.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_005.text: The next bundle belonged to a worker who had already received wages among the nineteen completed claims. His personal property was still in the hold. Yue checked the separate references, resisting the temptation to place him among the thirteen just because he now waited at the same gate. He had brought a receipt proving payment and a description of his boots. The boots were found beneath a canvas roll. He held them against his legs to test the height, smiling like a man who had recovered a small piece of winter.

harbor_p03_006.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_006.text: Sui Yan permitted cleaned, cleared personal items to leave only through the recorded collection process. The commercial clerk gave notice for competing claims and set a short review for ordinary belongings whose description and custody were supported. The captain did not keep safe coats behind the fence because a tub's title remained disputed. Miao complained that removing items would make the inventory incomplete. Han Pei, present for the worker references, pointed to their recorded disposition. A completed line did not require the physical object to remain forever beside it.

harbor_p03_007.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_007.text: By midday, Yue's coat smelled of wet rope despite her dry position. She washed her hands before eating, as the captain instructed all workers near the sorting shed. Yan Su bought a bowl of noodles and spilled half the broth while trying to wave a gull away. Bo announced that the gull had better authority over the lunch table than the foreman. Yan Su laughed and moved his bowl indoors. The crew's jokes were not evidence that danger had passed. They were people reclaiming an ordinary break between careful tasks.

harbor_p03_008.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_008.text: A small chest arrived after the meal, its hinges corroded and its lid tied with a strip of old sail. Fen recognized the sail stripe from a bag her father had carried. She had come only to ask whether a letter arrived. The commercial clerk kept her outside the work line and asked for her description before opening the chest under recorded handling. Fen named a chipped cup and a pair of spare cuffs. Both were inside. So was a folded wage contract bearing Luo Jian's fuller name.

harbor_p03_009.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_009.text: The find seemed to promise an answer about her father until Sui Yan showed the transfer note attached beneath the tie. The chest had been left aboard for delivery to shore storage after he passed inspection. Its presence did not prove he had stayed on the vessel. Fen read the note herself, lips moving over each word. She had built a hopeful version of the discovery in the time it took the chest to cross the shed. Now she put that version away without denying that the contract could still help.

harbor_p03_010.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_010.text: The contract copy could establish Luo Jian's wage terms even while the safe-contact search continued. Fen requested a witnessed copy for the wage inquiry. The original remained in the inventory custody until its rightful recipient could collect it or the proper representative process was completed. Nobody placed the chest in Fen's arms simply because she knew its contents. She touched the outer sail strip from the permitted side of the table, then asked the clerk to keep it with the chest. Her father had mended that strip himself.

harbor_p03_011.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_011.text: Han Pei compared the contract with the shortened wage line and confirmed the link using the recorded name evidence. Luo Jian's amount could now be calculated. The recipient remained unresolved; Fen's contact request was not a wage appointment. The girl asked whether the money would disappear while she waited. Qin Shuo supplied a written hold reference and review route. It preserved that claim without deciding death, abandonment, or inheritance. Fen folded the page around her ticket. Paper had become heavy enough to need its own pocket.

harbor_p03_012.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_012.text: Later in the afternoon, two tub markings turned the commercial shed into a place of raised voices. Miao claimed the tubs for his merchant because their current paint matched the purchase invoice. A container lender named Wen Zhi produced an older drawing showing an incised maker's mark under the paint. The clerk stopped the argument long enough to request a safe inspection of the base. Yan Su's crew turned the emptied, cleared tub on its approved cradle. The old mark was there, surrounded by recent blue brush strokes.

harbor_p03_013.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_013.text: The mark supported the lender's claim about the container's identity. It did not prove who owned the remaining contents or whether a later sale had transferred the tub itself. Wen Zhi demanded immediate return. Miao demanded that the invoice be treated as conclusive. The clerk entered both documents for comparison and left the tub held. Yue heard the anger rise at the table beside her and understood why separate records were necessary. She also understood why the people shouting thought separation sounded like a way to postpone surrendering anything.

harbor_p03_014.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_014.text: He Ming asked Miao whether the containers had been sold before the voyage. He said the merchant had bought a mixed lot, including tubs that might once have belonged to others. She pointed out that might was not a purchase record. He answered that a packer did not know every commercial agreement. He Jun stepped forward, ready to defend his sister. Yue caught his eye from the dry table. The woman was defending herself. He stopped, then found another place to put the anger in his hands by folding the recovered coat.

harbor_p03_015.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_015.text: After the first inventory day, the captain's clean-item releases included He Jun's coat and spoon. No competing claim had been filed within the ordinary collection process, and the described bundle matched the recorded custody. He signed for both under his own property reference. He Ming watched him put on the coat. It made him look less like the exhausted stranger at the fish steps and more like the brother she had imagined. She was annoyed by how easily clothing could change her mood toward somebody whose answers remained incomplete.

harbor_p03_016.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_016.text: The inquiry term gave Yue another paid shift the following morning. She used it to compare the worker bundles with the relevant wage lines, not to investigate cargo title. Han Pei worked beside her and grew quieter as a pattern emerged. Several hiring addresses came from one yard clerk's batch, though the people had lived elsewhere for years. Each carried the same notation: household not presented. Yue asked whether that phrase had been copied into the public unclaimed list. Han Pei looked back through the page history before answering.

harbor_p03_017.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_017.text: The phrase had traveled. It began on a shore hiring summary, entered the voyage wage register as an unresolved address field, and appeared in the current list as a reason a recipient could not yet be verified. The records did not show who chose each step's meaning. Han Pei had inherited the summary and written the public heading herself. She could account for that last act. The earlier acts needed their own sources. Yue wrote the chain as a question rather than a verdict against a conveniently absent yard clerk.

harbor_p03_018.speaker: harbor_han_pei
harbor_p03_018.text: I know what I did when the list reached this desk. I left the old address because I expected the households to come and correct it. Some did. I took that as proof the method worked. The ones who could not come became the unresolved remainder. It is easy to say I should have noticed earlier. I did notice a problem. I treated it as their missing information instead of asking whether our starting address was one any household had ever used.

harbor_p03_019.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_019.text: The admission did not end the inquiry. Han Pei sent the source question to the former yard office under her own name. Yue carried the public request during a scheduled outreach shift, with the necessary receipt and no private household letters. The yard gate stood inland behind a row of new dye vats. Its old sign had been turned inward. A tenant told her the former hiring clerk no longer worked there. The current manager had retained some records in a storeroom because nobody had agreed who should pay to move them.

harbor_p03_020.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_020.text: The manager let Yue see the public transfer inventory. Wage and hiring books were listed in a locked cabinet, with custody assigned to the harbor office after the old yard lease ended. They had not actually been delivered. Yue asked him to acknowledge receipt of the source request and contact the named harbor keeper. She had no authority to break the cabinet seal. The manager seemed relieved to have a specific demand rather than another visitor telling him the records were important. He promised a reply by the next working afternoon.

harbor_p03_021.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_021.text: On the walk back, Yue passed the former sleeping sheds. They now held indigo cloth stretched over frames. A woman rinsing a vat said workers had once slept there during busy weeks but families rented elsewhere. Old Salt Yard was a place of work, not a common household address. She would give that account if asked, but she would not speak for every former worker. Yue recorded her willingness and contact point with permission. The indigo water in the drain made the empty yard seem full of a different season.

harbor_p03_022.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_022.text: He Ming knew the sleeping sheds and had never thought to mention them. They were where she rested between night packing shifts. Her mother had visited once and refused to stay because the beds smelled of fish oil. If somebody had asked whether the yard was her address, she would have said it was where a foreman could find her during a job. Nobody had asked with enough precision for that difference to appear. Yue read the new question aloud. He Ming answered with visible relief and a trace of shame.

harbor_p03_023.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_023.text: At supper, the woman said the inquiry made her feel as though she should have known how to speak correctly from the beginning. Yue said the office had responsibility for making its questions usable. He Ming replied that responsibility did not keep her from feeling foolish. She put the last piece of fish into Fen's bowl when the girl arrived. Fen said she had been asked to distinguish a father's family name from a hiring name as though she had invented the confusion herself. The three women ate without solving that feeling.

harbor_p03_024.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_024.text: A reply from Reed Steps arrived on the fourth week's first morning. Fen's father had been seen at a lodging house there after his west-creek passage. The lodging keeper had forwarded her letter to a nearby timber camp where he sought work. No reply from him had yet returned. Fen asked why he had gone inland when his coat and cuffs remained in a chest at the harbor. Yue did not know. The news moved the search closer to a person while opening another piece of his life that the girl had not expected.

harbor_p03_025.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_025.text: Fen wanted an inquiry journey to Reed Steps. Yue checked the appointment scope with Han Pei and the route cost with the pilot. A permitted outreach visit could seek status and carry the contact request, without compelling disclosure of the father's address. It would cost six copper for ordinary return ferry travel within the twenty-four ceiling. Fen could travel on her own fare if her support arrangements permitted; her presence was not purchased by Yue's appointment. The girl consulted the support clerk and arranged a safe overnight option before deciding.

harbor_p03_026.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_026.text: The journey could not occur until the following week because Yue's two scheduled shifts were already assigned to source records and inventory. Fen hated the answer but listened when Han Pei offered to send another letter immediately through the reopened route. She chose both: a letter now, a planned visit later. It was the first time she had accepted that one useful step did not replace another. Yue marked the travel proposal pending its ordinary approval. The ferry money remained in the inquiry account, not in her purse.

harbor_p03_027.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_027.text: At the quay, the inventory prepared for a second day. More personal bundles lay beneath tubs whose handling required different precautions. The crew could bring only a limited set into the dry shed before the tide reached the working mark. Yan Su proposed splitting the public support tasks so none of the three waiting areas lost its assigned person. Yue could take one post. Ordinary staff would take the others and submit their records. Han Pei wanted her at the comparison table. He Ming wanted her beside the claimant queue.

harbor_p03_028.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_028.text: The request surprised Yue because He Ming usually asked for the result rather than Yue's presence. The woman said some workers trusted a stranger who had listened before a clerk who knew the rules. Han Pei looked hurt and tried to hide it by arranging forms. Yan Su needed someone at the dry work line who would repeat a direction without embellishment. Each request had a practical reason and a personal hope. Yue could not honor all three by arriving with four extra hands. Her inquiry shift contained one body's time.

harbor_p03_029.speaker: lin_yue
harbor_p03_029.text: Tell me what the post requires today, and what another person can do there. I will choose one. I have seen the danger of making every good intention depend on the same person. Han, your table needs an accurate comparison. He Ming, your queue needs people heard without promising an answer nobody can give. Yan, your line needs clear instructions and ordinary discipline. We should agree on who covers the other two posts before the crew opens the gate. Then my choice will be a task rather than a rescue of everybody's confidence.

harbor_p03_030.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_030.text: The clerk, claimant delegate, and foreman named the ordinary staff covering the unchosen posts. Their reports would enter the same inventory file with sources visible. Yue looked from the blank forms to the waiting workers, then toward the haul rope drying on its rack. Each place offered a different view of the day. None offered authority over the whole operation. She would choose where to spend her paid half-day, knowing the choice would change what she understood firsthand and which person would feel she had stood beside them.

choices.text: Work beside Han Pei at the comparison table.
Take Yan Su's dry work line.
Stand with He Ming at the claimant queue.

harbor_p03_031.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_031.text: Yue stayed at Han Pei's comparison table. The clerk handed her a bundle-description sheet that had been copied before the first inventory. Two entries carried the same family reference but different recipients. Yue caught the duplication while the objects were still inside the controlled shed. They checked the original descriptions with the owners, who confirmed that one household number had been reused for a different worker. No property had yet left under the wrong name. Han Pei wrote the correction and asked Yue to check the fresh copies aloud.

harbor_p03_032.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_032.text: The comparison brought a young man to tears. He had feared that claiming a bundle under his hiring number would erase the name his mother used. Han Pei let him write that name beside the linked record, identifying it as his supplied family form. She did not make one cancel the other. Yue watched the clerk's shoulders ease as the man signed. He Ming's criticism had hurt because it touched something true. This time, accuracy gave the clerk a way to remain at the table without becoming less human there.

harbor_p03_033.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_033.text: Miao sat across from them while a description of a tool roll was checked. He said the roll belonged to the merchant because the tools had been used aboard. Han Pei asked for the purchase or employment term supporting that claim. He found no such term in his current packet and agreed to seek it rather than demand release. Yue wrote the pending question and its response date. He said her handwriting made him feel accused. She showed him the neutral wording and asked which sentence misrepresented his request.

harbor_p03_034.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_034.text: By the end of the table shift, the corrected household number and the tool-roll question had clear records. He Ming's ordinary queue assistant supplied the attendance notes, while Yan Su's relay clerk supplied the work-line account. Yue had not watched those tasks. Han Pei thanked her for helping catch the number before release. Yue understood something new about the clerk's guarded manner: defending a table could be an attempt to stay useful, especially when everyone arriving remembered only what the table had failed to give.

harbor_p03_035.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_035.text: Yue chose the dry work line with Yan Su. The foreman marked her position and rehearsed the spoken relays before the haul began. A visiting agent tried to step inside the line for a better look at his tubs. Yue stopped him and repeated the designated viewing route. He complained that she had no power to exclude an owner. Yan Su confirmed the work boundary applied regardless of ownership. The man moved back, furious but safe. Yue felt the effort of holding an ordinary limit without adding a cultivator's threat.

harbor_p03_036.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_036.text: When the crew brought up a cleared tool roll, its tie snagged against a splinter on the shed threshold. Yue saw the haul rope begin taking the twist and called the instructed stop. The rigger stopped at once. Yan Su freed the tie by hand from the dry side after the load was supported. Nothing dramatic followed. That was the point he made when Bo called it a small interruption. A prevented accident rarely supplied the noise people used to recognize a useful warning.

harbor_p03_037.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_037.text: During the next break, Yan Su asked why Yue had chosen his line. She said she wanted to understand the work behind the inventory sheets, not just the claims written after objects reached the table. He showed her the marker positions without offering the rope controls. The lesson made the cargo delay look different. Every safe handoff required time, space, and a crew who could hear one another. A merchant's frustration did not make those needs disappear. Neither did Yue's sympathy for a cold man waiting on his coat.

harbor_p03_038.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_038.text: At the shift's end, Han Pei supplied a signed correction note about a reused household number, and the queue assistant supplied the claimant account. Yue had not observed those exchanges. Yan Su recorded her stop call beside the harmless snag it addressed. He thanked her without calling her indispensable. On the walk to the office, Yue noticed her throat hurt from repeating instructions above the wind. She had learned a different kind of fatigue from the quiet table, and she did not confuse either with a higher cultivation stage.

harbor_p03_039.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_039.text: Yue took the claimant queue beside He Ming. The woman introduced her to workers whose property descriptions had arrived through several different hands. One man spoke little harbor speech and kept handing over a paper meant for his landlord. Yue checked the appointment's interpreter line before asking the ordinary language desk for a bounded session. Its clerk arranged an hour at the established rate. The man could identify his own bundle once he heard the questions clearly. His confusion had never been evidence that he lacked a claim.

harbor_p03_040.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_040.text: A woman named Dai Min asked whether collecting her husband's boots would sign away his unpaid wages. He Ming had feared the same thing about her brother. Yue showed the property receipt's purpose and asked the commercial clerk to explain its exact effect. It acknowledged collection only. Dai read the wording herself before agreeing to the description check. The queue moved slowly while each person understood what a signature did. He Ming watched and stopped urging Yue to hurry, though the next tide still pressed against their available time.

harbor_p03_041.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_041.text: When a cleared bundle failed to match its claimant's description, Yue did not encourage him to accept it because it was similar. He identified a different buckle and said his own strap had been repaired with green thread. The clerk kept the bundle held and searched the remaining inventory references. The man left disappointed but with an accurate receipt for the unresolved claim. He Ming said she would once have called that a wasted afternoon. Now she thought of the person whose bundle might otherwise have vanished into another household.

harbor_p03_042.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_042.text: The comparison table sent a signed correction about a reused household number; Yan Su sent a report of a stopped snag at the work line. Yue had observed neither. Her own shift ended with a six-copper interpreter charge entered against the twenty-four-copper ceiling, leaving eighteen available. He Ming thanked her for standing where people began. Yue said the queue would continue needing ordinary staff after her term. The woman agreed, then asked her to stay for supper anyway. The invitation belonged to a friendship rather than the appointment.

harbor_p03_043.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_043.text: The three posts' records met at the north office that evening. The reused household number had been corrected before any affected property release. A harmless snag had prompted the instructed stop, and a confused claimant had received interpretation through the language desk. Yue's own report identified the post she had taken; other signed notes identified what she had not witnessed. The day supplied no universal proof that a table, queue, or rope line mattered most. It showed how easily one missing task could make the others seem careless.

harbor_p03_044.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_044.text: The ordinary language desk's six-copper charge covered the same bounded hour whether Yue had attended the queue or read its report afterward. Han Pei entered it once against the inquiry interpreter ceiling, leaving eighteen copper available. The payment belonged to the whole operation, not to a reward for a chosen post. Yue checked the remaining expense lines before closing her shift: copying had used two copper, ferries had used none yet. The coming Reed Steps journey would need its approved fare before any departure.

harbor_p03_045.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_045.text: Across all posts, the inventory produced a sealed packet from the old hiring yard. Its outer address named the harbor office, but its internal delivery mark showed it had been placed with crew bundles at departure. Nobody had meant to send it aboard, according to the ship agent's initial account. That explanation required checking. The captain recorded the packet's condition and transferred it through authorized custody to the wage clerk. The cargo process had found a possible source without deciding what its contents meant.

harbor_p03_046.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_046.text: Han Pei waited for the named keeper before opening the packet. Inside lay household address slips and a covering instruction from the old yard's hiring clerk. It directed staff to use the yard address on outward lists because collecting individual lodging addresses took too long during departure. The slips contained actual lodging points for several of the thirteen households. They were not proof that those families still lived there. They were proof that useful contact information had existed before the public list described the households as unresolved.

harbor_p03_047.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_047.text: He Ming's slip named the room she had left before the voyage, not the temporary packing lodging she used now. Her brother's line named a different shore inn. Han Pei did not publish either. She could use the old points to seek current safe contact through the approved process. Yue felt anger at the packet's journey through the hold. It had made a simple search harder for everyone. She also knew anger was not an explanation of whether the misplacement was accidental, careless, or intended.

harbor_p03_048.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_048.text: Miao said the packet must have been swept into cargo with the departure rush. Wen Zhi accused him of hiding household claims so the merchant could recover the bond. Qin asked each to identify a source. Miao named the loading supervisor who tied the packet into a canvas roll. Wen Zhi had no direct witness, only the commercial interest. The custodian recorded the factual lead and the allegation separately. An obvious benefit to somebody could justify a question. It could not supply the missing act in the answer.

harbor_p03_049.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_049.text: The loading supervisor was no longer at the harbor. The ordinary office inquiry sought his account through the recorded next workplace, preserving the packet and covering instruction in the meantime. The current wage decisions did not wait for his answer if contract and recipient evidence already sufficed. Han Pei sent newly useful safe-contact questions through the relevant keepers. Yue watched five old lodging addresses become five current questions. The manuscript of the harbor grew less mysterious, but the effort required to turn a line into a human reply remained substantial.

harbor_p03_050.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_050.text: At dusk, Han Pei closed the cabinet and put her key on the cord inside her coat. She looked suddenly young. She had spent years believing she could make a sound record by refusing to invent an answer. Now she had found an earlier answer trapped in a bundle, and understood how refusal alone could preserve another person's mistake. Yue asked whether she wanted supper. The clerk said she wanted to walk somewhere no one could hand her a paper. They went to the shore path without their office boards.

harbor_p03_051.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_051.text: The path passed a row of small boats overturned for repair. Han Pei counted them unconsciously, then laughed at herself. She had once wanted to become a boat painter. Her aunt said letters offered cleaner work and steadier pay. The ink on her fingers suggested the cleaner part had been overstated. Yue asked whether she still painted. Han said she drew birds in the margins of discarded forms, then cut the margins off before anyone saw. She sounded ashamed of an ordinary pleasure that had survived a sensible choice.

harbor_p03_052.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_052.text: Yue bought a scrap of clean paper from the stall at the path's end with her own coin and placed it between them on the seawall. Han Pei drew a gull badly, then another better. Yue drew the kite fish from the repair shed, complete with its claim to own the sea. Han laughed so hard she had to stop shading. The paper had no official purpose. They carried it back together anyway. Its existence made the evening feel less borrowed from a task that would resume in the morning.

harbor_p03_053.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_053.text: The following day, the former yard manager delivered the retained hiring books under the recorded transfer. The cabinet seal matched the inventory, and the harbor keeper entered custody before opening it. The household address slips in the shipboard packet corresponded to references in one of the books. A separate column tracked permit fees for lodging workers. Several household entries had been marked yard housed though the yard collected no corresponding bed charge. Yue flagged the mismatch. The book contained a question about administration, not yet a conclusion about a scheme.

harbor_p03_054.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_054.text: The administrator authorized a separate permit review through the proper desk. Yue's wage task could report the relevant mismatch, but her appointment did not expand into collecting fines or questioning every former tenant. Han Pei continued the wage calculation. He Ming said the workers should not have to wait for the yard's fee problem to be solved. Qin agreed that their earned claims had their own evidence. The new review might affect responsibility for bad addresses. It did not turn contracted work into an unearned favor from the merchant.

harbor_p03_055.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_055.text: At the commercial shed, Wen Zhi produced a signed tub-loan agreement. It identified six containers by maker's mark and allowed their use for one voyage, with return after safe clearance. Miao's purchase invoice described contents packed in six tubs but did not expressly transfer the containers. The commercial clerk gave the merchant a chance to identify any later agreement. Miao frowned at the papers, then requested time to ask his employer. He no longer demanded that fresh paint erase the older mark. The dispute had become more specific and less loud.

harbor_p03_056.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_056.text: He Jun wanted to leave the harbor as soon as his coat dried. He Ming wanted him to wait until their mother arrived. Their quarrel returned beside the fish steps, where the first meeting had occurred. This time, He Ming said what she feared: she would become the person receiving letters after every departure while he remained the person allowed to begin again. He Jun said he would not promise never to leave. He could promise a real collection point and write before changing it. She hated how modest that sounded.

harbor_p03_057.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_057.text: Yue met He Jun later at the repair shed's water barrel. He asked whether his sister had told her everything about the loan. Yue said the family conversation did not belong in her wage report. He seemed relieved, then disappointed because he wanted her to judge him kindly. She would not offer that shortcut. He described his partnership's failure without naming the private creditor. Yue listened, thinking how many people came to a stranger hoping for a version of themselves that their families no longer allowed.

harbor_p03_058.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_058.text: Fen's second letter from Reed Steps arrived before the planned journey. It was written by the timber camp's cook, who had read her father's earlier message aloud to him and sent his dictated reply. Luo Jian had injured two fingers in a saw mishap after taking camp work. He was receiving ordinary care and had chosen not to worry his daughter until he knew whether he could return to loading. The cook enclosed a current witnessed mark. Fen read the explanation with rage growing where relief had begun.

harbor_p03_059.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_059.text: Her father said he would write again when the dressing came off. Fen wanted to write that he could have sent one line sooner. The tea seller advised waiting until she was less angry. Fen asked Yue whether anger made a letter unkind. Yue said it depended on what she chose to say with it. Fen wrote three versions, tearing none of them because paper cost money. In the final version, she said she was glad he lived and that his silence had hurt her. Both statements fitted on one page.

harbor_p03_060.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_060.text: The planned outreach journey remained useful if Luo Jian consented to the contact visit and record comparison. Lian Zhou forwarded the proposed meeting without giving Yue an unapproved private address. The cook's public camp collection point could receive the request. Fen still wanted to travel. The support clerk reviewed her safe lodging arrangement and ordinary route, without treating her father as dead or appointing a new guardian. Yue expected the reply before the ferry day. No one promised that a family could be repaired by reaching the correct bank.

harbor_p03_061.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_061.text: On the fourth week's last afternoon, the wage custodian authorized the second verified payment group of one hundred sixty-eight copper. The decision included claims whose recipient questions had been resolved through the new contact sources and direct accounts. Actual payments were recorded separately as people collected them. When the group finished collection, the bond balance fell from six hundred six to four hundred thirty-eight copper. Supported wages still unpaid totaled two hundred twenty-four. The remaining claims included Luo Jian's held amount and other unresolved recipient details.

harbor_p03_062.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_062.text: He Ming took no additional money from the second group; her own paid receipt remained in the first. She attended as a claimant delegate with specific permission from two neighbors who wanted her to hear their reasons read aloud. One neighbor could not attend because she had found a washing job. Her chosen collection route preserved the payment without demanding another lost shift. He Ming began to understand the work Han Pei did each day. Understanding did not excuse the unclaimed heading. It made their disagreement less easy to enjoy.

harbor_p03_063.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_063.text: The two women met outside the office afterward. He Ming apologized for implying that every claimant trusted a stranger more than the clerk. Han Pei said some did, and asked what would make the desk easier to approach. He Ming proposed a chair outside the window for people whose questions took longer than the queue allowed. Han said a chair needed somebody assigned to answer it. They agreed to raise the idea at the term review rather than let the object become a promise on its own.

harbor_p03_064.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_064.text: Deren returned from the care house using a crutch, furious that the tide had continued in his absence. The port injury process had paid its prescribed immediate treatment support while the accident review proceeded. His longer loss-of-work claim remained under review with his shift record preserved. Yan Su met him at the dry gate and showed the removed brace. Deren ran his finger near the rotten patch without touching its splintered edge. He asked why nobody had lifted the patch sooner. Yan Su said that was the question the review needed him to answer.

harbor_p03_065.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_065.text: The injured worker wanted his old post back before the clinician allowed it. Yan Su refused the platform assignment and offered to ask about a compatible seated stock-checking task through ordinary employment. Deren accused him of replacing danger with uselessness. The foreman looked away. Yue knew the sentence had struck the place where his dead brother still stood. He answered that the task could be useful and paid, but Deren could refuse it. A restricted ankle did not become a permit for either unsafe pride or unpaid sympathy.

harbor_p03_066.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_066.text: Bo began helping Deren with the stock list after his regular shift, until the foreman asked who had authorized extra hours. Bo said he was doing a favor. Deren said he did not want to become somebody's favor. They arranged a short paid overlap through the ordinary maintenance schedule, with a clear end. Yue watched the older worker regain his temper as he corrected Bo's rope measurements. The argument became almost cheerful. Competence had found a place where it did not require Deren to climb a wet step.

harbor_p03_067.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_067.text: At the captain's shed, the next cargo notice cleared one group of sacks after controlled treatment and inspection. Other material remained held for disposal review or ownership questions. Sui Yan signed the technical findings; the commercial clerk signed permitted releases after title review. The documents carried separate authorities. Miao collected no tubs still disputed under the loan agreement. He did collect cleared goods whose sale rights were supported. Movement finally occurred, and the harbor's impatient stories adjusted themselves to pretend they had expected exactly this result.

harbor_p03_068.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_068.text: A small festival began on the first clear evening of the fifth week. Its drums found the right rhythm at last. The repair shed's boy flew the fish kite from the dry square, with Yue holding the ordinary spool while he untangled its tail. He Ming brought pears. Han Pei brought the gull drawing, carefully folded away from office papers. Yan Su arrived late with Deren, who complained about every uneven paving stone. The captain stayed near her duty route but accepted a piece of pear when the boy offered it.

harbor_p03_069.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_069.text: Fen came after the tea stall closed. She watched the fish rise and asked whether its owner had won the sea. The boy said ownership was still disputed because the gulls refused to sign. She laughed before remembering she was angry with her father. Yue saw relief return to the girl's face without pretending anger had vanished. He Ming gave her a pear, and Han Pei showed her the ugly first gull as well as the better second. For an hour, none of their missing information sat at the center of the table.

harbor_p03_070.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_070.text: Late that evening, Luo Jian's consent to the contact visit arrived through the camp collection point. He would meet them at the public cookhouse on the agreed ferry day. His private lodging address remained undisclosed. Fen read the note, then placed it beside the kite spool so she would not lose it. Yue checked the travel approval the following morning: six copper ordinary return fare charged to the ferry ceiling, with the remaining eighteen held for later authorized journeys. Fen's separate fare and overnight arrangements were confirmed before they left.

harbor_p03_071.speaker: narrator
harbor_p03_071.text: Yue packed for the creek journey with the same personal things she had brought to the harbor. The loaned inquiry board and authorized comparison forms traveled under a written checkout, to return afterward. She carried no cargo sample, no ward stone, and no power to command the timber camp. The inquiry would ask about Luo Jian's wage recipient and preserve his answer if he wished. Fen's reunion belonged to her own journey. At the west landing, the pilot counted passengers in an ordinary voice while spring sunlight moved across the thawed water.
